version_note: Bump this whenever a field is added/removed/renamed, a column_order changes, or a unit/encoding rule changes. Every value stored downstream (Contract 2/3) should record which schema_version produced it -- otherwise a schema change later makes old stored predictions impossible to audit correctly. v1.1.0 changes from v1.0.0: fixed Gut column_order to match actual CSV sequence; separated Age/Gender into shared_features (previously miscategorized as metadata).
_notes: Source of truth for the preprocessing unit's feature mapper. Labels are NOT included here on purpose -- they are the model's OUTPUT, not input, and appear only in training CSVs, never in this schema. 'metadata_fields' contains ONLY Patient_ID -- a pure identifier, never a model input. 'shared_features' contains Age and Gender -- these ARE real model inputs (present in every model's column_order), just identical across all three models so defined once instead of three times. Every feature has a 'source' that tells the mapper how to obtain it: 'report_extraction' (search uploaded documents, ask user only if missing/out-of-range), 'user_form' (always a direct question, never searched for in a document), or 'system_generated' (never touched by the mapper -- assigned by the platform itself). A model only fires if every 'required': true field in its column_order resolves to a valid value or is confirmed unavailable (in which case that model is excluded from fusion for this run, not sent partial data).
design_decision_kept_declarative: Reviews suggested adding regex patterns and complex matching rules directly into this schema. Deliberately NOT doing that -- this file describes WHAT each field is (type, unit, range, aliases), not HOW to find it in messy text. Matching logic belongs in the mapper's code/Matching Engine (see contract_2b_feature_mapper_pipeline.json), which can be tested/versioned/debugged like normal code.
valid_range_clarification: Every 'valid_range' in this schema is a PLAUSIBILITY range (catches OCR misreads and extraction errors), NOT a clinical reference/normal range. Real extreme-but-true values exist (e.g. ALT can genuinely reach 800+ U/L in acute hepatitis) and must not be rejected -- ranges here are set wide enough to allow genuine medical extremes through while still catching obvious extraction errors (e.g. HbA1c=65 from a misread decimal).
conflict_threshold_note: Per external review: a single global 20% threshold is wrong for medical data -- HbA1c changing 10% is clinically significant, Weight changing 1% is not. 'default_conflict_relative_threshold' above is the fallback for any field without an explicit override. Fields below with an explicit 'conflict_relative_threshold' override that default. NOTE: only the clinically highest-priority fields have been explicitly tuned so far (HbA1c, Systolic/Diastolic BP, Weight) as a demonstrated pattern -- a full clinical review to set appropriate thresholds for every remaining field is still recommended before production use.
canonical_unit_note: Every field's 'unit' value (already present throughout this schema) IS the canonical_unit referenced in Contract 2/3 -- i.e. the target unit a value is converted TO, not necessarily the unit it arrived in. No separate field needed; 'unit' already serves this purpose and is used as such downstream.

Patient_ID.note: Assigned by the platform (account/session ID). Never searched for in a report. Never fed to any model -- pure identifier only.

shared_features._note: Age and Gender are real input features (not metadata) -- they appear in EVERY model's column_order and directly affect predictions. Defined once here since identical across Clinical, Wearable, and Gut.

Gender.encoding_note: FINALIZED. This exact mapping must be used in BOTH the training script (df['Gender'].map({'Male': 1, 'Female': 0}), not LabelEncoder -- LabelEncoder picks alphabetically and could silently give the opposite mapping) and the feature mapper's Gender encoding step. This schema file is the single source of truth for the mapping -- both places should read from here rather than hardcoding it twice.

Height_cm.unit_note: Reports may give feet/inches (e.g. 5'10") or meters. Detect unit from the text and convert to cm before storing.

Weight_kg.unit_note: US-sourced reports/scales often use lbs. Detect and convert to kg before storing.

BMI.derive_note: If not found directly, auto-compute instead of asking the user.
BMI.derive_rounding_policy: Round to 1 decimal place using standard round-half-up (e.g. 25.849 -> 25.8, 25.85 -> 25.9). Store the full-precision computed value in 'converted_value' per Contract 2, and the rounded value in 'values' -- this matches how the training CSV's BMI column was almost certainly generated, so rounding must match to avoid a systematic offset between training-time and inference-time BMI.

Waist_Circumference_cm.unit_note: Often reported in inches on US forms. Detect and convert to cm.

Systolic_BP.extraction_note: Rarely listed as a separate labeled field. Usually appears as a single combined reading like 'BP: 128/82 mmHg' -- parse and split into Systolic (first number) and Diastolic (second number).

Diastolic_BP.extraction_note: See Systolic_BP -- comes from the same combined 'sys/dia' reading, second number.

Fasting_Blood_Glucose.unit_note: International reports often use mmol/L. Detect and convert to mg/dL (mg/dL = mmol/L x 18.0).
Fasting_Blood_Glucose.fasting_status_note: MANDATORY confirmation rule: if the matched alias text does not explicitly contain the word 'fasting' (e.g. report just says 'Glucose' or 'Random Glucose'), the mapper must NOT accept the value as Fasting_Blood_Glucose automatically -- treat it as unresolved and confirm fasting status with the user before storing, since a non-fasting reading is a different clinical measurement entirely.

HbA1c.unit_note: Some countries report IFCC units (mmol/mol) instead of NGSP % (e.g. 48 mmol/mol = 6.5%). Detect and convert to %: % = (mmol/mol / 10.929) + 2.15.

LDL_Cholesterol.unit_note: Detect and convert to mg/dL (mg/dL = mmol/L x 38.67).

HDL_Cholesterol.unit_note: Detect and convert to mg/dL (mg/dL = mmol/L x 38.67).

Triglycerides.unit_note: Detect and convert to mg/dL (mg/dL = mmol/L x 88.57).

Family_History_Diabetes.question_text: Does a close blood relative (parent/sibling) have diabetes?
Family_History_Diabetes.form_note: Direct Yes/No question shown to the user. Never searched for in an uploaded report. No 'unsure' option -- only Yes or No.

Family_History_Obesity.question_text: Does a close blood relative (parent/sibling) have obesity?

Family_History_Hypertension.question_text: Does a close blood relative (parent/sibling) have high blood pressure?

Family_History_NAFLD.question_text: Does a close blood relative (parent/sibling) have fatty liver disease (NAFLD)?

wearable.source_note: Two supported paths, user's choice: (1) 'device_sync' -- live connection via a free API (e.g. Google Fit, Fitbit Web API) or a self-hosted aggregator (Open Wearables); (2) 'report_extraction' -- manual file upload (CSV/export), same document reader pipeline as Clinical/Gut. If the user has no wearable device at all, Wearable model is skipped for that run (same rule as Gut) -- fusion proceeds with whichever of Clinical/Gut are complete. Whichever path is attempted, the same missing-field question, out-of-range reject-and-reconfirm, and all-or-nothing completeness rules apply.

Average_Glucose.unit_note: Detect and convert to mg/dL (mg/dL = mmol/L x 18.0).

gut.availability_note: Gut microbiome sequencing is a specialized test many users won't have. Platform should display upfront, before upload, which named test to bring (e.g. 'Gut Microbiome Test / stool sequencing panel'). If unavailable, Gut model is skipped for that run -- fusion proceeds with whichever of Clinical/Wearable are complete.
